punchline: The Mongol post was fast because nobody ran far.
thirty_sec: In Marco Polo's description of the Mongol yam, post-houses stood about every twenty-five miles, foot-runners with bell-hung belts changed every three miles, and express riders took a fresh horse at each station. The speed came from the prepared handoffs, not from any one fast runner.
question: At which handover in your work does something regularly go missing?
key_contrast: Speed from prepared handoffs, not from one fast runner.
